competitors.name: peon-ping
competitors.strengths: THE strongest competitor. 21 harness adapters (Claude Code, Amp, Copilot, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Kilo, Kiro, Kimi, Windsurf, Antigravity, Rovo, DeepAgents, Qwen, iFlow, Trae, ECA, +). Ships FIVE Agent Skills (peon-ping-config/-log/-rename/-toggle/-use), a CLAUDE.md, a GEMINI.md, an MCP server where the agent picks the sound via play_sound, a ~60-command non-interactive CLI, Homebrew tap, install.sh/install.ps1, community sound-pack registry, 4 README languages, own domain peonping.com, macOS Focus/DND + headphones_only + meeting_detect auto-mute, overlay banners, per-directory and per-IDE pack binding. Show HN scored 1006 points / 301 comments on 2026-02-12.
competitors.weaknesses: Collapses every lifecycle event into 7 sound categories (session.start, task.acknowledge, task.complete, task.error, input.required, resource.limit, user.spam) — no per-tool-type granularity. No status line. Windows parity incomplete (setup/rotation/preview/mobile not yet supported). WSL2 audio path is fragile on Win11 24H2+ (needs ffmpeg). Identity is a Warcraft joke, which caps enterprise/professional adoption.
competitors.positioning_vs_you: Theirs is funny, everyone has heard of it, and it installs with `brew install` — and you configure it by talking to your agent, exactly like ours. Ours makes a different noise for 39 distinct events instead of 7 categories, and adds a status line. Buyer-visible difference: they pick a character, we pick a lifecycle event.

kills_your_moat.why: Its skills/peon-ping-config/SKILL.md description reads 'Use when user wants to change peon-ping settings like volume, enable round-robin, add packs to rotation, toggle sound categories, or adjust any config' — that is echook's 'natural language forever' mechanism, in echook's exact niche, at 63x the stars. The 'AI-operated' claim is dead on this single artifact.

competitors.name: Abandoned twins cohort (convergent-invention evidence)
competitors.stars_or_installs: scv-sounds 41★ (dead 2025-08-15) · CCNotify 216★ (dead 2025-10-14) · Claude-Code-Remote 1275★/135f (dead 2025-12-06) · claude-code-notify-powershell 92★ (dead 2026-01-11) · ai-notifier-swift 13★ (dead 2026-01-21) · Claude-Code-Notifier 94★ (dead 2026-02-01) · claude-code-notif-manager 39★ (dead 2026-02-13) · game-sounds 86★ (dead 2026-04-14) · agent-manager-x 72★ (dead 2026-05-05) · codevator 63★ (dead 2026-05-31) · tallr 25★ (dead 2026-06-18)
competitors.strengths: Collectively 2,016 stars and 200+ forks of demonstrated interest. Capable people independently identified the same gap between Aug 2025 and Jun 2026.
competitors.weaknesses: All silent for 6-12 months. Most plausible cause: Claude Code added 13+ hook events in 8 months and an unmaintained notification tool silently stops covering the lifecycle it advertises. Alternative cause that cannot be ruled out: Anthropic documented the free fix and closed issue #1288 as 'completed' on 2025-08-22.
competitors.positioning_vs_you: Eleven people built this and stopped. echook is one of the few in the cohort still shipping — but its last push (2026-07-19) is older than nine active competitors', so 'still shipping' is the honest phrase, not 'the maintained one'.

kills_your_moat.why: This is the superlative-free argument: convergent invention proves the gap was real; survival is checkable via last-commit dates. It does NOT support 'the only maintained one' — claude-hud, ccstatusline, code-notify, agent-tools, Lucarne, agentbro and anotifier all pushed more recently than echook.

competitors.name: The 5-line DIY hook (Anthropic's own documentation)
competitors.category: substitute that is not a product — the true price ceiling
competitors.price: $0. Zero lines in Ghostty/Kitty/iTerm2 (built-in desktop notification); 3 lines for {"preferredNotifChannel": "terminal_bell"}; 9 lines for the official afplay Notification hook; ~15 lines for the official 3-platform desktop-notification hook
competitors.stars_or_installs: n/a — first-party docs. Corroborating DIY trail: 7 blog posts opened (2025-07 to 2026-06, 11-24 config lines each) and 20 gists found across two fetched search pages, 4 opened
competitors.strengths: Free, first-party, zero install, and it is the FIRST thing a user finds — the docs page's own symptom index literally reads 'No sound or alert when Claude finishes'. Anthropic closed feature request #1288 'Sound notifications' (44 reactions) as COMPLETED on 2025-08-22, pointing at preferredNotifChannel and hooks. Every echook capability has a $0 substitute: TTS = macOS `say`; toasts = osascript / notify-send / BurntToast (1,724★ MIT); webhooks = ntfy.sh (free, no signup); sound = afplay (pre-installed).
competitors.weaknesses: One sound, one event, one OS. No per-event mapping, no debounce, no mute, no cross-platform path. Demonstrably breaks in real setups: anthropics/claude-code#8985 'Notification hook doesn't work in VS Code extension native UI mode' has 65 reactions; #5186 'Notification Hook 10 second delay' has 32.
competitors.positioning_vs_you: Theirs is nine lines you paste once and never think about. Ours is a package that maps 39 events across three editors — which only matters if the nine lines break, and whether they break is unmeasured.

kills_your_moat.why: Caps willingness-to-pay at $0 permanently. Corroborated by revealed demand: the three npm packages that ARE the 5-line version packaged pull 2, 1 and 6 downloads/week; code-notify (280★) pulls 41/week. The only path back to nonzero WTP is proving the free hook has a high real-world failure rate.

competitors.name: Claude Code platform (hooks, statusline, notifications, /statusline, Agent Skills)
competitors.strengths: 31 documented hook events; 8 Notification matchers (permission_prompt, idle_prompt, auth_success, elicitation_dialog/_complete/_response, agent_needs_input, agent_completed) — echook's event taxonomy as a config string. preferredNotifChannel accepts sound/vibration/visual/none/terminal_bell. terminalSequence hook output emits OSC 9/99/777 + BEL without a controlling terminal. Statusline is handed pre-computed context_window.used_percentage (2026-01-13) and rate_limits 5h/7d + resets_at (2026-03-19). CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE (2026-06-17) is a first-party snooze. /statusline accepts natural-language instructions and writes the script and settings for you. Surface expanded by 13+ hook events and 8+ statusline fields in ~8 months.
competitors.weaknesses: No per-event sound mapping, no theme packs, no TTS, no debounce, no cross-harness install. Mobile push requires a claude.ai Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise login and is unavailable on Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, with a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, with API-key auth, or for ZDR orgs — a real, documented gap.
competitors.positioning_vs_you: Theirs is already in the box and the docs tell you how in nine lines. Ours is what you install when nine lines are not enough — and the platform's own demand data says most users do not think they need more (sound feature requests: 1, 1, 0, 0 reactions; notification requests: 69, 65, 42).

kills_your_moat.why: Both echook tracks have first-party equivalents; the statusline numbers are pre-computed so echook's bars are formatting, not measurement; and /statusline already does natural-language configuration of a local tool by an agent — in echook's own domain.

competitors.name: Cursor platform (21 agent hooks + third-party Claude-hook execution)
competitors.strengths: 21 documented agent hook events including `stop` ('Handle agent completion'), plus Tab and app-lifecycle hooks; hooks.json at user/project/team/enterprise scopes. Verbatim: 'Cursor can load and execute hooks configured for Claude Code, allowing you to use the same hook scripts across both tools' — loading .claude/settings.local.json, .claude/settings.json and ~/.claude/settings.json, and automatically mapping Claude hook names to Cursor equivalents.
competitors.weaknesses: ZERO notification/sound documentation — cursor.com/llms.txt has no notifications page and /docs/configuration/notifications, /docs/settings/notifications and /docs/agent/notifications all 404. The widely-reported in-app 'play sound on finish' setting could NOT be verified against any Cursor-official URL — UNVERIFIED, claim in neither direction.
competitors.positioning_vs_you: A user who installed echook for Claude Code already has audio in Cursor via a compatibility checkbox. Our Cursor adapter competes with a toggle.

kills_your_moat.why: Erodes 'one install covers three editors' — Cursor absorbs Claude hooks natively. It does NOT create Cursor's 21 native events or per-tool-type granularity, which echook targets directly. The toggle's default state is unverified.

competitors.name: OpenAI Codex CLI (notify + tui.notifications + tui.status_line)
competitors.category: platform absorption — most absorbed of the three
competitors.strengths: `notify` config invokes an external command with a JSON payload (type, thread-id, turn-id, cwd, input-messages, last-assistant-message) and the docs ship a working terminal-notifier example. tui.notifications (bool or event array), tui.notification_condition (unfocused|always — a native snooze), tui.notification_method (auto|osc9|bel — a native terminal bell), and tui.status_line (an ordered, user-configurable native status line — Codex did in config what Claude Code did via a script contract). 11 hooks in deliberately Claude-compatible PascalCase.
competitors.weaknesses: `notify` currently emits ONE type, agent-turn-complete — the narrowest per-event gap of the three platforms, and the one place echook's granularity has the most headroom. No bundled sound. tui.status_line item identifiers not enumerated in the docs (UNVERIFIED).
competitors.positioning_vs_you: Theirs bells and shows a status line from a config file with no install. Ours distinguishes a failed tool from a permission prompt, which `notify` cannot do at all.

kills_your_moat.why: Absorbs the sound, the snooze and the status line natively — but its single notify event type leaves echook's per-event granularity genuinely unmatched on Codex.

competitors.name: Anthropic Agent Skills / Plugins (the 'AI-operated' pattern itself)
competitors.category: platform absorption — prior art for the headline claim
competitors.stars_or_installs: 601,280 files named SKILL.md and 168,544 named AGENTS.md on GitHub (gh api search/code, 2026-08-04)
competitors.strengths: Published 2025-10-16, verbatim: 'Skills are authored for agents rather than humans', 'organized folders of instructions, scripts, and resources', 'Skills can also include code for Claude to execute as tools at its discretion'. The Claude Code skills doc ships a worked example of echook's exact architecture — allowed-tools: Bash(${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/render.sh *) — so a skill can drive a bundled CLI without a permission prompt. /statusline and /fewer-permission-prompts are first-party natural-language settings configurators. Plugin roots put bin/ on the agent's PATH by design; /plugin install is the documented one-command install.
competitors.weaknesses: None relevant — this is the platform defining the pattern.
competitors.positioning_vs_you: There is no buyer-visible difference. This is how the platform says to build this, and echook is built that way.

kills_your_moat.why: 'AI-operated, not AI-assisted' and 'you don't read this, your agent does' paraphrase Anthropic's own published definition of the primitive echook ships. Cite these docs as evidence that echook is CONFORMANT — never as evidence that it is novel.

competitors.name: agents.md + llms.txt (agent-readable docs conventions)
competitors.category: platform absorption — prior art for 'your agent reads this'
competitors.stars_or_installs: agents.md: 'used by over 60k open-source projects'; 168,544 AGENTS.md files on GitHub
competitors.strengths: agents.md is backed by OpenAI (Codex), Google (Jules), Cognition (Devin/Windsurf), Anthropic (Claude), JetBrains (Junie), GitHub (Copilot) and ~20 more, and is 'now stewarded by the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation'. llms.txt (Jeremy Howard, 2024-09-03) states 'we expect many of these files to be read by language models and agents'.
competitors.weaknesses: n/a
competitors.positioning_vs_you: Shipping an AGENTS.md and an llms.txt is what every project does now; it is not a stance.

kills_your_moat.why: 'You don't read this documentation, your agent does' was a published convention 23 months earlier and is now a Linux Foundation standard.
